title: EDGE-A1594 3v3 Defensive-Zone Positioning Game
source_text: Divide players equally into two groups along the blueline. Two defenseman and one forward defend against three forwards below the tops of the circles. If the puck comes out of the zone or a goal is scored quickly, the coach can add another puck. Shifts should last 30 seconds.
game_problem: Defend three attackers below the tops of the circles with coordinated positioning, support, and quick reaction to continued play.
representative_information: Puck location, three attacking forwards, defender/forward support, net, circle-top boundary, possession outcome.
player_decisions: Defenders and the supporting forward read puck location and attacker spacing to protect dangerous space, pressure, and support each other.
space_organization: Below the tops of the circles with 3 attackers versus 2 defensemen plus 1 defending forward; coach can add a new puck when play ends quickly.
coach_notes: Keep the play live and positional; do not prescribe who must pressure. Let puck location and attacker spacing drive coverage decisions.
adaptation_text: Use the source 30-second shift. On a quick goal or puck exit, immediately add another puck as written to preserve repeated defensive reads.
source_boundary: Player numbers, area, new-puck rule and 30-second shift are source-derived. Decision-language and coaching emphasis are Carolina EDGE framing.

title: EDGE-A1339 Net-Front Coverage Transition Game
source_text: Net Front Coverage Game - 2v2 in each part of ice and players must stay on their sides. On each side there are 2 defenders and 2 offensive players. Defenders try to get puck to other side to their offense. FOCUS on picking up a man to cover in the D zone and getting open in ozone.
game_problem: Defend net-front threats, win possession, and transition the puck to teammates in the opposite half.
representative_information: Assigned side, two attackers, two defenders, net-front threats, possession change, teammate availability across the divider.
player_decisions: Defenders identify and cover threats, then choose how to move the puck to the other side; offensive players find space to receive and attack.
space_organization: Rink divided into two halves; 2v2 in each half, with players staying on their side and two nets shown.
goalie: GOALIES NOT CLEARLY SPECIFIED IN SOURCE TEXT
coach_notes: Preserve the side restriction because it creates repeated coverage and transition reads without turning into a skating route.
adaptation_text: Restart immediately after goals, puck exits, or stalled possession so both halves get repeated defensive-coverage and transition moments.
source_boundary: 2v2-per-side structure, side restriction, defender-to-offense transition and source focus are source-derived. Restart guidance is Carolina EDGE adaptation.

title: EDGE-A1198 2v2 Forecheck vs Retrieval Game
source_text: Coach shoots puck into one of the corners. D1 and D2 proceed in to retrieve puck. In a staggered fashion, F1 and F2 forecheck on their side. The idea is that Defense partners make a quick pass and shoot out of Zone, or Fwds steal puck. FWD that is not attacking goes to net for pass and shot. Drill is over when defense clears or Fwd's shoot on net.
game_problem: Two defenders retrieve and exit under a staggered two-player forecheck while forwards read whether to pressure or support the net.
representative_information: Dump location, defender support, staggered forechecker pressure, passing lane, net support, possession outcome.
player_decisions: Defense reads pressure and chooses a quick support pass/exit; forwards coordinate pressure, with the non-attacker supporting the net for a pass and shot.
space_organization: Half/end-zone 2v2 retrieval-forecheck game starting from a coach dump into either corner.
coach_notes: Vary the dump side and forechecker timing. The forecheck should create the problem rather than a prescribed chase route.
adaptation_text: Run to the source end condition: defensive clear or forward shot on net. Restart from the opposite or same side based on the next desired read.
source_boundary: Coach dump, D1/D2 retrieval, staggered F1/F2 forecheck, support-to-net behavior and end condition are source-derived. Variation guidance is Carolina EDGE adaptation.

title: EDGE-A1427 Perpetual Forecheck Transition Game
source_text: 3 Fs and 2D in zone, 3 Fs go around circle and coach dumps in so other team gets it but 3 Fs can forecheck 1-1-2 or 2-1-2. After puck is cleared by defensive team, they go around circle and go in as forecheckers on the team that was just forechecking. Continuous.
game_problem: Transition continuously between breakout/retrieval and forecheck roles after a defensive clear.
representative_information: Coach dump, possession, defensive clear, teammate/opponent positioning, forecheck structure, role change.
player_decisions: Forecheckers coordinate pressure and support within the selected forecheck structure; the defending group retrieves and exits, then immediately transitions into forecheck after the clear.
space_organization: Half-ice/end-zone continuous forecheck game with 3 forwards and 2 defensemen in the zone; next group activates after the clear.
coach_notes: Treat 1-1-2 or 2-1-2 as structural options, not fixed routes. Players should still read puck location and pressure.
adaptation_text: Keep the drill continuous as written and rotate groups so all players experience retrieval, breakout support, and forecheck transition roles.
source_boundary: Player numbers, coach dump, forecheck structure options, clear-triggered role reversal and continuous format are source-derived. Rotation emphasis is Carolina EDGE adaptation.
